327474.title: Generalized commuting probability determines central quotient order
327474.scope: If Pr^{2n}(G1)=Pr^{2n}(G2) for every n>=0 then |G1/Z(G1)|=|G2/Z(G2)| (Conjecture 6.3 of arXiv:1403.3868v2).
327474.why: Cheap decisive calculations exist: Pr^{2n} computable by direct enumeration for small groups (n<=3 at |G|<=16 verified here); counterexample would be two explicit groups + computed sequences + differing central quotient orders. Source gives the tools (Theorems 6.1/6.2, class-multiplicity formula). Risk: no counterexample may exist at small order; equality for all n needs a structural certificate (e.g., identical class-multiplication tables).
327474.decisive_next_calculation: Full small-group scan (all groups of order <=64, GAP SmallGroups or equivalent): compute (Pr^2,Pr^4,Pr^6), find equal-sequence pairs, compare |G/Z|; then certify equality for all n structurally. Pilot scan here (D8..D8xC3, order<=32, n<=3) found only isoclinic pairs with equal sequences and equal |G/Z| - consistent with the conjecture, no cheap refutation.
327474.certificate: Refutation: two groups + sequences + class tables (small, Lean-able via explicit enumeration). Affirmation: hard/unbounded.
327474.formal_deps: Finite groups by explicit Cayley tables; rational sequence comparison; no advanced libraries.
327474.evidence_level: primary_body_read (arXiv:1403.3868v2 HTML full text, Conjecture 6.3 + Theorems 6.1/6.2 retained in sources/)
327474.successor_note: arXiv:2605.02071 (2026, 'Higher Commutativity in Finite Groups') and the signed-Hultman follow-up (10.1007/s10801-021-01089-9) are closest successor literature; neither screens as answering Conjecture 6.3; dedicated prior-art pass still required.
